newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-NO DANGER OVER OLYMPICS, SAYS SAMARANCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO DANGER OVER OLYMPICS, SAYS SAMARANCH.

text.p: International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch said on Friday he was not worried by threats to withdraw soccer from the summer games.

"There hasn't really been any danger that the sport could disappear from the Olympics," said Samaranch. He stressed the great respect to the Olympic movement shown by FIFA president Joao Havelange, who has criticised both soccer's role in the Olympics and the organisation of the Atlanta tournament.
Havelange had said in an interview earlier this month that soccer had gained nothing financially from the Atlanta Games and could be pulled out of the Olympics if it continued to be "marginalised."
Meanwhile, Samaranch, 76, confirmed on Friday he would announce in March whether or not he would stand for re-election.
"I really love this job ... the happiest time of the day for me is when I open the door of my office in the morning," he said.
